_readme: Seed tickets for Mintlify's 'Update docs from tickets' automation. Create them in Linear (team key DEMO, or map ids) by hand or with the Linear API; nothing here is created automatically. Each ticket names the code repo and the files (code there, docs in mintlify-demo/docs under /<repo>/) so the agent has context; the same mapping is in each repo README under 'Ticket -> file map'. Suggested demo: move a ticket to Done after merging its code change, and Mintlify opens a docs PR.

tickets.title: Reject sort requests over 10,000 numbers with 413
tickets.description:
Large lists make `/sort/steps` responses several MB and slow the free instance down.

**Change**
- `POST /sort` and `POST /sort/steps` return `413 Payload Too Large` with `{"detail": "At most 10000 numbers per request"}` when `numbers` has more than 10,000 items.
- Document the limit and the error in the API reference and in the Sorting at scale guide.

**Acceptance**
- Test for 10,000 (ok) and 10,001 (413).

tickets.title: Send Sunset and Deprecation headers on every v1 calculator response
tickets.description:
v1 is being retired on 2027-01-31 (see the deprecate-v1 PR). Clients should learn that from the responses, not only from the docs.

**Change**
- Every `/v1/*` response includes `Deprecation: true` and `Sunset: Sun, 31 Jan 2027 00:00:00 GMT`, plus `Link: </v2/calculate>; rel="successor-version"`.
- Document the headers in the OpenAPI responses and in the v1 overview and v1 vs v2 guide, with a migration table.

**Acceptance**
- Tests assert the headers on all four v1 endpoints and their absence on v2.

tickets.title: Recurring todos
tickets.description:
Customers want todos like "Send the weekly report" to come back after they're done.

**Change**
- New optional `repeat` field: `daily`, `weekly`, or `monthly` (default none).
- Completing a repeating todo creates the next one with the same title and repeat, and the response includes `next_id`.
- Expose `repeat` in GraphQL (`Todo.repeat`, `CreateTodoInput.repeat`).
- New guide: Recurring todos.

**Acceptance**
- REST and GraphQL tests; `the docs PR` regenerated openapi.json and schema.graphql.

tickets.title: Rate limits per plan with X-RateLimit headers
tickets.description:
Plans should differ in more than bulk import.

**Change**
- Per-key limits per minute: standard 60, partner 300, enterprise 1,000.
- Every response has `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
- Over the limit: `429` with `Retry-After`.
- Document limits in the Authentication guide (table per plan) and the 429 response on every endpoint.

**Acceptance**
- Tests for the headers and the 429 path (use a tiny limit via env var).

tickets.title: Add a todo.completed event to the WebSocket stream
tickets.description:
Partners only care when a todo is finished, and today they have to diff every `todo.updated`.

**Change**
- When `completed` flips from false to true, send `todo.completed` (same payload as `todo.updated`) in addition to `todo.updated`.
- `subscribe` accepts `todo.completed`.
- Add the message to the AsyncAPI spec and the event table in the Event stream page.

**Acceptance**
- WebSocket test; asyncapi.yaml lists the new message (the existing test checks EVENT_TYPES against it).

tickets.title: Stop-word filtering for /word-count
tickets.description:
Word counts are dominated by "the", "a", and "and".

**Change**
- Optional `ignore_stop_words` (bool, default false) on `POST /word-count`; when true, `unique_words` and the counts skip a built-in English stop-word list.
- Response adds `stop_words_ignored` (int).
- Update the x-codeSamples and the Examples guide.

**Acceptance**
- Tests for both modes; `the docs PR` regenerated.
